feedback.end:
Under their white fur, polar bears have black skin to help them soak up warmth from the sun.

In order to survive the harsh winters, polar bears sleep in caves for 4 to 5 months every year. This is called hibernation.

Walruses have a thick layer of fat that keeps them warm in the cold water.

They also have two long teeth coming out of their mouth, called tusks. Throughout their lives, their tusks never stop growing.

The Arctic fox lives in an underground cave it digs itself, called a den. Its den has many tunnels to help the fox get around.

It also has thick fur that keeps it warm in the cold Arctic environment.

atoms.a: The Arctic is snowy all year long.
There are icebergs in the Arctic.
There is at least one day a year when the Arctic has sun all day long.
